assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins is a foundational physical-chemical result: tunneling-mediated rates across defined distances, with driving force and reorganization energy tested in ruthenium-modified proteins. It gives a quantitative physical framework for biological redox chains, which is the kind of mechanism I value most.
assessment.attribution: The decisive experimental program is Gray and Winkler's, with a clean two-person configuration. Marcus theory was recognized in 1992, so this builds on a recognized theory without duplicating it. Others (e.g. Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton on tunneling-pathway models) contributed, but the credit is more clearly bounded than in most candidates.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and wide use in respiratory and photosynthetic enzyme work, including hopping mechanisms. The field is stable, and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a continuation of the 1992 Marcus prize rather than a new achievement.
Pathway-model contributions by others may be raised against a two-person award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer links theory and catalysis: concerted proton-electron transfer, its theoretical description, and applications in water oxidation and fuel-forming electrocatalysis. It is central to bioenergetics and enzyme mechanisms, including cytochrome c oxidase-type chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Mayer (concept and thermochemistry of PCET), Hammes-Schiffer (theory) and Nocera (biomimetic and catalytic PCET) form a plausible trio. Thomas J. Meyer's early contributions and the split between theory and catalysis leave allocation of credit unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are mature and widely accepted, and the applications are active. The catalytic component is less settled than the mechanistic one.
uncertainties: The candidacy combines fundamental mechanism, theory and device-oriented catalysis, so the contribution is diffuse.
Meyer's priority could displace one of the three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism concerns how biology reduces N2 at a unique metal cofactor (FeMo-cofactor). Structures including the central carbide, together with kinetic and spectroscopic work on the E4 state and electron-proton delivery, address a long-standing chemical problem of major importance.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle provided the structural determinations of the protein and cofactor. Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe contributed mechanism and biochemistry. A three-person award would exclude significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: The structural results are reproduced and well accepted. The catalytic mechanism is still debated, so the recognition could be premature for the mechanism but not for the structure.
uncertainties: Unresolved N2 binding and reduction mechanism.
Allocation among structural versus biochemical contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new chemical modality that redirects the ubiquitin-proteasome system, and it is now clinically validated. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained a long-standing drug mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the heterobifunctional degrader concept; Handa identified cereblon. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and others made large contributions, so a three-person limit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are advancing and mechanistic confirmation is strong. Approved degrader drugs remain few, so a later date might be safer.
uncertainties: Number of deserving contributors exceeds three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled structures from nanocrystals before radiation damage, and time-resolved structures of reacting proteins. It makes biochemical dynamics visible, which suits my interest in methods that show mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the conceptual and methodological demonstration and the data-analysis frameworks. Fromme, Schlichting and Hajdu added crystal sample delivery and applications. The method crosses into physics and instrument development, which complicates the attribution.
assessment.maturity: Method is validated across many facilities. Time-resolved results on enzymes are still maturing, so impact on chemistry is growing rather than established.
uncertainties: Whether the chemical discoveries are sufficient yet.
Availability and role of Hajdu in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional NMR for large biomolecules, including triple-resonance, TROSY-based and relaxation methods, opened structure and dynamics of proteins in solution. Millisecond-timescale dynamics and sparse excited states connect structure to function.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are central. Wüthrich's 2002 prize covered the early structural methodology, so the later developments must be distinguished clearly as separate contributions.
assessment.maturity: The methods are universally adopted and stable. Timing is not an issue, but novelty relative to 2002 will be scrutinized.
uncertainties: Distinguishing contributions among Bax, Clore, Kay, Wagner and Palmer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves intact noncovalent protein complexes in the gas phase, which allows stoichiometry, subunit interactions and ligand/lipid binding to be read out. It shows assembly states of membrane proteins and respiratory complexes that other methods find difficult.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is the leading figure for membrane protein complexes, Heck for instrument and application development, and Chait for early approaches. Credit overlaps with 2002 (Fenn, Tanaka) for the ionization methods, so the new contribution lies in complexes.
assessment.maturity: Methods are widely used and independently confirmed. Whether gas-phase structures faithfully reflect solution structure is a known caveat.
uncertainties: Which of the several pioneers is decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory of protein folding recasts Levinthal's paradox with funneled landscapes, a physical principle that explains folding kinetics and robustness. Experimental mapping, for instance by Fersht, tests the picture.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the central originators of the funnel framework, and Dill contributed lattice models and the hydrophobic-collapse view. Bryngelson and Fersht make a clean three-person grouping difficult.
assessment.maturity: The theory is widely accepted conceptually, but some predictions are hard to test directly. It is more a framework than a specific discovery.
uncertainties: Conceptual framework rather than a single discovery.
